question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Bone to pick

options.text: To be angry about something and want to discuss it

solution: The correct answer is: **To be angry about something and want to discuss it.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Bone to pick"** means to be angry or annoyed about something and want to discuss it. (किसी बात से नाराज होना और इसे चर्चा करना चाहना) • **Example: **She called him because she had a bone to pick about the way he handled the project. • **"To be angry about something and want to discuss it"** means feeling upset or agitated about a particular issue and having the desire to talk about it. (किसी बात से नाराज होना और इसे चर्चा करना चाहना) • **Example: **John had a bone to pick with his colleague about the missed deadlines. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. To be angry about something and want to discuss it. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **To stop trying hard** (कड़ी मेहनत करना बंद करना): To give up or cease putting in effort. • **Example:** He decided to stop trying hard after facing multiple failures. • **To not give up** (हार नहीं मानना): To persist or continue despite difficulties. • **Example: **Even when things got tough, she decided to not give up. • **Putting in extra effort** (अतिरिक्त प्रयास करना): To work harder than usual. • **Example:** He was putting in extra effort to ensure the project was completed on time. 42:Tbae, The correct answer is: **nothing**.
